speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative check-up. To better understand your shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty, can you tell me how many weeks ago you had your surgery and if the pain is worse on one side or both?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your history of bilateral ear infections, your right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago, and the specific symptoms of shooting pain triggered by eating and discomfort with earrings, I need to evaluate the integrity of the graft and the tympanic membrane.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Tympanic Membrane Perforation with Possible Chondritis or Graft Failure
